name: ZMA
lead: ZMA is a supplement combining zinc, magnesium and vitamin B6, marketed to athletes, gymnasts and bodybuilders. It was developed by Victor Conte, the founder of BALCO Laboratories [1]. The standard formulation contains zinc monomethionine aspartate, magnesium aspartate and pyridoxine hydrochloride (vitamin B6) [1].

Its marketing centres on taking it before bed to support sleep and anabolic (muscle-building) processes. Published studies are few and conflict: a 1998 company-linked study reported strength gains in football players, while later studies found no effect on testosterone or performance [1]. In looksmaxxing communities it is discussed as a sleep and testosterone support supplement.
infobox: Zinc monomethionine aspartate, magnesium aspartate, vitamin B6 [1]

paras: The original product pairs 30 mg zinc, 450 mg magnesium and 10.5 mg vitamin B6 per serving, and the manufacturer advises taking it on an empty stomach 30 to 60 minutes before bed, avoiding calcium because of claimed absorption interference [1]. SNAC holds the trademark but the formula is not patented, so other brands sell similar products [1]. Variants include ZMA-5, which adds 5-HTP and is sold as a sleep aid; Wikipedia notes 5-HTP can raise serotonin, which may affect sleep, appetite and body temperature [1].

A 1998 study of NCAA football players over eight weeks of spring training found that those taking ZMA gained more muscle strength; it was funded by SNAC Systems, and co-author Victor Conte holds equity in the company [1]. A 2004 study funded by Cytodyne tested a ZMA-containing product (Z-Mass PM) and found no significant effects on hormones, strength, endurance or sprint capacity [1]. A German study reported that ZMA altered urine colour through increased zinc excretion, with no effect on testosterone [1].

ZMA is commonly grouped with sleep and testosterone-support supplements in bodybuilding and ascension discussions. Published research cited on Wikipedia reports mixed results, and funding sources of the studies have been noted as a point of controversy [1].

timeline.event: Study in NCAA football players reports greater strength gains with ZMA; funded by the trademark holder [1]
Industry-funded study of a ZMA-based product finds no significant effects [1]

card.summary: A zinc, magnesium and B6 night-time supplement sold for sleep and testosterone; the few studies conflict.
card.aka: Zinc magnesium aspartate + B6, Z-Mass PM
card.note: Key supporting study was funded by the trademark holder.

quick.overview:
ZMA is a bundle of zinc, magnesium and vitamin B6, created by BALCO founder Victor Conte and sold to athletes as a pre-bed supplement.

A 1998 company-funded study reported strength gains, while later studies, including an industry-funded one, found no significant hormone or performance effects.
quick.mechanism: The claimed idea is that these minerals support sleep and anabolic hormone processes, with timing before bed intended to improve absorption.
quick.risks: Sold as a dietary supplement. Variants add 5-HTP, which can raise serotonin. Published safety data are not extensively covered in the available sources.
